subject.title: [Feature]: Memory durability config — hard flush threshold, priority-aware compaction, cache TTL

question: Should OpenClaw add public runtime/config contracts for hard token-based memory flush, priority-preserving compaction metadata, and embedding-cache TTL, and should those land together or be split?
rationale: The source-level config gaps are clear, but the request adds public memory and config semantics in a session-state area where owner boundary, upgrade behavior, and user-visible durability guarantees need maintainer intent.

options.title: Split Contract Decisions
options.body: Approve, reject, or narrow hard flush, priority preservation, and cache TTL independently so each can get focused schema, runtime, docs, and validation work.

options.title: Accept The Bundle
options.body: Treat all three knobs as one production memory durability feature and require a broader design PR covering every schema and runtime surface together.

options.title: Defer New Config Surface
options.body: Keep the current soft flush, transcript-byte forced flush, safeguard compaction, and content-hash cache behavior until narrower failure evidence justifies each new public knob.

recommendation.title: Split Contract Decisions
recommendation.body: Approve, reject, or narrow hard flush, priority preservation, and cache TTL independently so each can get focused schema, runtime, docs, and validation work.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for memory flush and memory-core ownership points to steipete, and the remaining blocker is product direction for these contracts.
